subject: Hospitality
title: The Art of Tableside Service
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Art of Tableside Service usable.

hook.text: Tableside Caesar salad preparation, flambéed desserts, and carved roasts—tableside service turns a meal into a live performance.

buildup.text: Tableside service peaked in the 1950s–70s, declined with casual dining, and is now returning as experiential dining gains appeal.

discovery.text: The performance adds perceived value: guests pay 20–40% more for tableside preparation. The theater justifies the premium.

twist.text: Tableside service requires extensive staff training and slows table turns. It's labor-intensive.

climax.text: Hotels are reviving tableside as a differentiator—creating moments that can't be replicated at home or ordered via an app.

punchline.text: Tossed, flamed, carved at your table. Tableside makes the server the show.

quiz.question: How much more will guests pay for tableside preparation?
